dataset: Admission model parameters per programme (C-tier-equivalent GPA, 4-point scale)
method: Scale: every admitted student's GPA is put on one scale by adding the first-degree tier offset (A +0.21, B +0.10, C 0), measured as the gap between tiers' admitted medians on the same programme (84 and 156 programmes).
Observed programmes (5+ reported admits): K = admitted median and theta = 25th percentile on that scale, shrunk towards the model prediction by sample size.

Programmes without reports: K, theta and spread predicted by a weighted ridge regression on the observed ones, with the institution's QS rank, the subject's best QS 2026 / ShanghaiRanking GRAS 2025 rank, discipline, degree type, country, the stated minimum class, IELTS, any-background entry, name features (generic management, environment/sustainability, quantitative), competitive wording, applications per place, and a partially pooled institution effect. Cross-validated on held-out institutions.

Elite: K >= 3.9 (where C-tier admits fall to about 5%) or 8+ official applications per place. Ceiling c: 0.8 for taught programmes; for elite ones 3 x the offer rate, capped at 0.9; never below the programme's own offer rate. The offer rate is places / applications / yield, with yield (offers that become enrolments) taken from Oxford's and Cambridge's published statistics for the programme's own department or School, else the two universities pooled (0.595 over two years); where the page gives no applications per place, the department's or School's published offer rate. A unit offer rate at or below 1 / (8 x yield) also marks a programme elite.

MBA: full-time MBAs with a school-reported acceptance rate (U.S. News data via Poets&Quants, data/raw/mba-admit-rates.json) take it as their offer rate, are elite at or below 1 / (8 x yield), and have ceiling c = 2 x the acceptance rate, capped at 0.9; other MBAs in the United States and Canada keep 0.8 instead of the GradCafe ceiling, which was fitted on MS programmes. MBA and executive programmes scale the chance by the applicant's full-time work: x1 from 2 years, x0.5 at 1 year, x0.2 below 1 year (Kaplan 360++'s rule; class profiles average about 5 years).

bgFactor: the C-tier share of admits at this K divided by its share at K = 3.8, fitted across programmes; applied to a C-tier or private-school applicant's chance. Below K = 3.8 it is 1 because the tier offset already accounts for the gap there; above it the 4.0 cap compresses the GPA gap and the background effect shows up as fewer C-tier admits instead.

Private-school offset delta (relative to the awarding university's tier) is estimated from Singapore private-school students' reported admits against the same programmes' overall admits, with a flat prior and a robust likelihood.

privateDelta.prior: flat on [-0.40, +0.15] relative to the awarding university tier; Student-t(4) likelihood

curveCalibration.note: GradCafe admits and rejections 2022+, 35 programmes; other countries keep the admits-only curve until rejection data exist

gre.evidence: GradCafe offers and rejections, same programme: +10 GRE points was worth +0.37 GPA in 2012-15 master's admissions (2,704 decisions, 107 programmes; international applicants +0.40) but only +0.13 in 2016-19 (264 decisions, 11 programmes). Since 2020 many programmes have made the GRE optional, and its weight is still falling; the rule is set below the older estimate for that reason.

taught.base: lowest IELTS minimum among the university's programmes

gmat.rule: read as a GRE total and scored with the GRE rule, weighted by the programme's GMAT status
gmat.classicToGre: inverse of ETS GRE Comparison Tool regression GMAT = -2080.75 + 6.38 V + 10.62 Q, sections equal: GRE = (GMAT + 2080.75) / 8.5

mbaWorkGate.note: full-time work years; unanswered counts as 0

mbaRates.source: School-reported figures in U.S. News & World Report 2026 Best Business Schools data, tabulated by Poets&Quants

global.formula: If the applicant's own class is below floor: not eligible (the programme's stated minimum, any route). Otherwise curve = c * sigmoid((gpa4 + tierShift[awarderTier] + delta + experienceBonus + max(greWeight * greBonus(GRE), gmatWeight * greBonus(GMAT as GRE)) + ieltsAdjustment - theta) / s), greBonus = 0.01 per GRE point from 325 to 335 plus 0.013 per point above 335, ieltsAdjustment = elite: -0.1 below IELTS 7.5, else 0; other programmes: +0.05 at 1.5 or more above ieltsBase; for an applicant at the floor band or above, P = max(curve, floorBandFactor * c * sigmoid((k - theta) / s)); between floor and mainRequirement the applicant is eligible only through the alternative route the page names. Multiply by bgFactor for a C-tier or private-school applicant, and on MBA and executive programmes by the work gate (experience.mbaWorkGate).

Singapore (Cambridge citizenship, 2024-2.note: Singapore is in the top ten for offers (114) but not for applications, so it had at most 369 applications (the tenth country's count).

ukOfficial.note: Offer rates by applicant origin are recorded as a check on bgFactor, not multiplied into the ceiling: most of the China-versus-all gap comes from applicants' GPAs and first-degree institutions, which the curve already counts.
